scope: Disposable GitHub-hosted Windows policy investigation and actual native-gateway preparation protocol. No customer installer or human speech acceptance claim.

interface_policy_without_driver_refresh.finding: Writing render-only mask 0x107 and the association to the two exact owned interfaces, followed by disconnect/reconnect, did not prevent default and communications output selection. Do not integrate this sequence as a verified fix.

limits: This is an isolated Windows CI experiment. The customer installer and production startup lifecycle have not yet integrated the sequence.

The initial unprepared attachment reproduced a temporary default-output change. This evidence establishes the state after preparation and after subsequent restart, not absence of all transient selection during first-time setup.
Only render-role default selection was prohibited. Capture remains selectable as a default input.
The check used generated PCM, not human speech.

production_protocol_initial_run.failure: CONFIGRET CR_NO_SUCH_DEVNODE during native preparation after detaching the initial unprepared device.
production_protocol_initial_run.correction: Treat disappearing device interfaces as absent; wait for the exact live PnP node to report DN_STARTED before policy writes and driver refresh, rather than accepting persisted interface keys as attachment readiness.

limits: The CI-only caller invokes the production Go preparation API and actual native gateway, but does not install or launch the LocalSystem platform service.
First unprepared enumeration temporarily changed output defaults. The verified invariant applies after preparation and during subsequent attachment/restart.
Generated PCM is not human speech; the matching unified installer still requires installation and service-lifecycle acceptance.

next_step: Build the matching unified Windows/Linux installers, verify Windows installation and the actual service lifecycle once, then publish the reviewed candidate with its remaining human-speech acceptance boundary. Keep CI-only programs outside runtime bundles.
